batchIdentityNotes.geometry: First decoded world-1400 feature is a multipolygon extending from Greenland across Scandinavia. Broad northern and Greenland coverage is not a settlement or effective-control map.
batchIdentityNotes.handling: Separate narrative from Denmark to Norway and modern Scandinavian cards; publicly distinguish interrupted rule and the imported endpoint.

batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded European coastal multipolygon, approximately 3.45 to 7.23 E, 50.73 to 53.62 N; no overseas possessions represented.
batchIdentityNotes.handling: Distinct from earlier Dutch Republic, Kingdom of Holland and modern Netherlands. Do not present 1806 to 1815 geometry as continuing Batavian institutions.

batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world-1800 polygon approximately 6.07 to 10.49 E, 45.82 to 47.81 N. The republic never included Geneva, Neuchâtel or the former Basel bishopric; Valais separated in 1802.
batchIdentityNotes.handling: Public endpoint warning. Existing Switzerland and Seven Zenden narratives remain distinct. Map geometry was inspected as a snapshot, not certified against every historical boundary.

batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world-1815 polygon extends approximately 18.77 to 20.26 E, 49.89 to 50.25 N, encompassing city and surrounding district.
batchIdentityNotes.handling: Separate from the city’s medieval history, Polish national states and the later Austrian Grand Duchy title. Publicly flags 1846 annexation despite 1878 imported endpoint.

batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world-1530 polygon lies in Valais, approximately 6.78 to 8.31 E, 45.86 to 46.47 N. It is a regional Valais outline, not the Dutch republic or a union of seven Swiss cantons.
batchIdentityNotes.handling: Opening distinguishes early district/bishop arrangement from republican sovereignty asserted in 1613 and consolidated in 1634. Context includes earlier water infrastructure explicitly dated. 1798 transformation supersedes imported 1800 endpoint; no unverified detailed frontier corrections.
